The facts are as under:
The deceased is the legally wedded wife of accused No.1 and their marriage was solemnised on 04.05.2007.
At the time of marriage, the accused persons demanded and received Rs.5 Lakh, 150 gms gold and Rs.10,000/- to purchase clothes as dowry.

After marriage, the deceased accompanied accused No.1 and both stayed in a rented house at Rameshnagar, Bengaluru.
After few days, the accused No.1 left the deceased to stay with the remaining accused persons.
At that time, accused persons started quarrel with the deceased, demanded additional dowry of Rs.25 Lakh, treated her with physical and mental cruelty.
The deceased told the same to C.W.1 to 4.
The panchayath was held and the accused persons were advised not to torture the deceased for dowry.
After sometime, the accused No.1 brought the deceased to Bengaluru and make rented house at Veerabhadranagar.
C.W.10 was the owner of the said house.
The accused No.1 on instigation of the remaining accused persons, again started to harass the deceased and demanded Rs.25 Lakh as dowry.
Without bearing the torture and dowry  5 S.C.No.79/2009 harassment, deceased consume multiple tablets on 05.09.2008 and admitted to Manipal Hospital.
On the same day she was discharged from the hospital.
On 06.09.2008, the deceased again complained of uneasyness and she was admitted to Columbia Asia Hospital.
On the same day about 2.15p.m, she breathed her last.
The accused persons are responsible for her death.
Hence this charge sheet.

The points that arise for my consideration are:
1. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that at the time of marriage of the accused No.1 with the deceased, the accused persons demanded and received Rs.5 Lakh cash, 150gms gold and Rs.10,000/- for clothes as dowry and thereby committed the offence punishable under Section 3 of D.P.Act?
2.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that after marriage,
the accused persons demanded additional dowry of Rs.25 Lakh and thereby committed the offence punishable under Section 4 of D.P.Act?
3.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that after marriage,
the accused No.1 left the deceased at his native place and all the accused persons with common intention started quarrel with deceased, demanded Rs.25 Lakh as additional dowry, after re-conciliation and advice by C.W.1 & 2, accused No.1 took a rented house belong to C.W.10 at Veerabhadranagar and at the instigation of the other accused persons, the accused No.1 harassed the deceased physically and mentally for not bringing additional dowry of Rs.25 Lakh and thereby committed the offence punishable under Section 498A r/w 34 of IPC?
4.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused persons with common intention, harassed the deceased by demanding additional dowry of Rs.25 Lakh, not tolerating the harassment, on 05.09.2008, deceased consumed multiple capsules, became unconscious, admitted to Manipal hospital,
Columbia Asia hospital and died while undergoing treatment and the accused persons are responsible for her death and thereby committed the offence punishable under Section 304B r/w 34 of IPC?
5. What order?
9.

My answer to the above points are as hereunder:
Points No.1 to 4 : In the Negative Point No.5 : As per final order for the following:

Points No.1 to 4:
All the points involve common discussion.
C.W.1 is a father of the deceased.
He is a complainant and he deposed as P.W.1.
He has stated that the accused persons demanded Rs.10 Lakh, gold ornaments as dowry, Rs.20,000/- each to the daughters, household articles worth Rs.1 Lakh and a two wheeler as dowry.
According to him, he paid Rs.5 Lakh to accused No.1 and Rs.15,000/- each to his sisters.
11. P.W.1 has stated that he sold a site in April 2007 for Rs.7, 50,000/-, borrowed Rs.2 Lakh loan on his P.F, hand loan from his relatives and mobilised the amount to meet the marriage expenses.
He has further stated that the accused persons with common intention used to harass his daughter and demanded additional dowry of Rs.25 Lakh.
He has again stated that the accused No.1 is a perverted man and tortured his daughter for one or the other reason.
12. P.W.1 has further deposed that many panchayaths were held and the accused persons never changed their attitude.
He has deposed that on 03.09.2008, about 10.30 a.m, his daughter had made a phone call and informed about the torture given by the accused persons.
He has again stated that on the same day about 9.30p.m, he came to know that his daughter is not feeling well and admitted to hospital.
According to him, the accused persons forcibly get discharged his daughter from the hospital.
He has further deposed that, he admitted his daughter to Columbia Asia hospital and she died on 06.09.2008.
Ex . P.1
is complaint.
The statement recorded by Thasildar is marked as Ex.P.2.
According to him, after 1 month of the death of his daughter, he noticed the death note in the hand bag of the deceased and handed over the same to the police.
The said letter is in Telugu language.
It is marked as Ex.P.3.
The markscard of the deceased is marked as Ex.P.4.
Marriage invitation card and marriage photos are marked as per Ex.P.5 to P.9 respectively.
13. The learned counsel for the accused has cross examined the complainant.
At that time, he has deposed his ignorance about E-mail ID of his daughter.
He does not know that his daughter was always used to send mail to her husband.
He has admitted that he was intended to perform grand ceremonial marriage of his daughter and he gave gold ornaments to his daughter and accused No.1 as a part of marriage rituals.
He has again admitted that he gave cash to sisters of accused No.1 as per the custom and tradition.
14. P.W.1 has admitted that the elders advised the accused No.1 and the deceased to lead happy marital life.
He has also admitted that his daughter and accused No.1 promised the elders to lead life in good terms.
He has admitted that, his daughter was admitted to Manipal hospital due to low BP.
15. P.W.1 has admitted that, at Columbia Asia Hospital, Doctor told that his daughter was died due to the consumption of multiple tablets.
The complainant has categorically admitted that he voluntarily paid Rs.5 Lakh to accused No.1 and there was no demand and receipt of dowry.
He does not know who wrote Ex.P.3.
He has admitted that the handwriting found in Ex.P.3 is not belong to his daughter.
16. It is worth to note that, in the later part of the cross-examination, the complainant has taken U- turn and denied the contents of the complaint.
He has denied the alleged cruelty and harassment by the accused persons.
He has admitted that, he deposed before the court as per the instructions given State Of Karnataka vs No.1 1.

17. C.W.3 has deposed as P.W.2.
She is the younger sister of the deceased.
Her examination in chief is the repetition of the testimony of her father.
At the time of time of cross-examination by the accused counsel, she has admitted that there was no demand and acceptance of dowry and her father voluntarily paid Rs.5 Lakhs to accused No.1.

18. C.W.2 is the mother of the deceased and she deposed as P.W.3.
Her evidence is the replica of the examination in chief of P.W.1 & 2.
During the cross- examination by the accused counsel, she has denied the dowry harassment, acceptance of dowry and the alleged cruelty and harassment.
She has admitted that her daughter was sensitive and she was leading happy marital life with the accused No.1.

She has failed to identify the handwriting in Ex.P.3.

reported the FIR as per Ex.P.13, conducted mahazar as per Ex.P.14, arrested accused No.1 and handed over the further investigation to P.W.25.

He does not know the reasons for the death of the wife of accused No.1.
According to him, the deceased was admitted to hospital due to her ill health.
22. C.W.25 has been examined as P.W.9.
He visited the place of incident and recorded the statement of witnesses.
He has collected postmortem report as per Ex.P.17.
The counsel for the accused persons has cross-examined the witness.
He has admitted that the deceased was admitted to Manipal hospital due to Migraine.
He has further admitted that she died immediately on the next day of her admission at Columbia Asia hospital.
He has again admitted that, her death was due to drug overdose.
23. P.W.9 has admitted that as per Ex.P.15, there was no antimortem injuries on the dead body.
He has admitted that as per the statement given by the witnesses, the relationship between the husband and wife was cordial and healthy.
24. C.W.19 has deposed as C.W.10.
He conducted postmortem and not found external injuries.
He reserved the opinion as to cause of death for want of chemical analysis report.
He has further stated that on 06.01.2009, he received FSL report and noticed the presence of Carbomate Insecticide in blood and viscera.
According to him, the death was due to respiratory failure as a result of consumption of substance containing Carbomate insecticide.

sentences.text: The counsel for accused persons has cross- examined.
He has admitted the requisition given by the police to conduct postmortem.
The said requisition is marked as Ex.D.1.
He has admitted that as per Ex.D.1, the deceased had consumed excess amount of unknown tablets on 05.09.2008 and admitted for treatment at CMS hospital, Manipal Hospital and Columbia Asia hospital.
He has further admitted that, in postmortem report, he has opined that, he was unable to give the specific cause of death.
26. P.W.10 has admitted that in case of consumption of wrong medicine which is poisonous in nature, there are chances of death resulting of respiratory failure.
He has again admitted that, his opinion as to cause of death is purely based on FSL report.
27. C.W.16 has bee examined as P.W.11.
He has conducted inquest in the presence of panchas and family members of the deceased.
He has recorded the statement of witnesses.
He came to know that the deceased was died due to consumption of poison.
Ex.P.16 is inquest.
The counsel for the accused persons has cross-
examined.
He has admitted that, Ex.P.16 was written by HAL police.
As per Ex.P.16, she was died at Columbia Asia hospital.
He has categorically admitted that, there are no materials to show whether someone had mixed poison in the food consumed by the deceased.
28. C.W.14 has been examined as P.W.12.
He has turned hostile.
He is not aware of contents of mahazar dated 07.09.2008.
According to him, he was not present at the time of mahazar proceedings and signed on a document at police station.
29. C.W.26 has deposed as P.W.13.
He collected report from FSL, completed the investigation and filed charge sheet.
At the time of cross-examination by the defence side, he has admitted that, he has not recorded the further statement of the witnesses.
30. C.W.15 has deposed as P.W.14.
He has identified his signature on Ex.P.14.
According to him, he signed on Ex.P.14 at police station and no mahazar was conducted in his presence.
He is not aware of contents of Ex.P.14.
He has failed to support the prosecution.
The prosecutor has cross-examined.

He has denied the contents of Ex.P.14.
31.
C.W.17 has been examined as P.W.15.
He has stated that on 05.09.2008, the deceased was treated in his hospital as out patient.
According to him, she was suffering from headache and not made complaint about any major health problem.
32. C.W.27 has deposed as P.W.16.
He has stated that on 13.10.2008, his office has received 4 articles and on 23.12.2008, he examined the said articles.
According to him, article 1 to 3 have responded for the presence of Methomyl insecticide.
He has deposed that article No.1 to 4 were destroyed after chemical examination.
He has again stated Methomyl insecticide is a type of insecticide and is not found tablet form.
Ex. P.18 is FSL report.
33. At the time of cross-examination by the defense counsel, he has admitted that after chemical examination, articles to be preserved and should be produced before the court as evidence.
He has further admitted that in Ex.P.18, it is not mentioned which method of test was adopted and what State Of Karnataka vs No.1 1.

B.R.K. Raja Yadav on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87276217/
8 result achieved in the form of color.
He has again admitted that, in Ex.P.18, it is not mentioned what standard sample was taken for examination.
He has further admitted that in Ex.P.18, he has not mentioned the ingredients of Methomyl.
34. From the above evidence, it is established that the wife of accused No.1 was died due to respiratory failure as a result of consumption of a substance containing Methomyl insecticide.
It is very strange that I.O has not found and seized alleged insecticide alleged as consumed by the deceased.
Though the complainant and his family members have supported the prosecution, at the time of cross- examination, they have categorically admitted that the deceased was in good terms with her husband.
They have further admitted that Rs.5 Lakh was paid voluntarily and there was no demand and receipt of dowry.
As per the evidence of P.W.10, there was no external antimortem injuries on the deadbody.
The witness has admitted that the deceased was admitted to Manipal hospital and Columbia Asia hospital with the history of headache and giddiness.
It is an undisputed fact that, the deceased was treated at CMS Hospital, Manipal Hospital and finally at Columbia Asia Hospital.
As per Ex.D.1, the deceased had consumed some excess amount of unknown tablets on 05.09.2008.
It is an undisputed fact that I.O has not recovered or seized the said unknown tablets alleged as consumed by the deceased.
Though as per Ex.P.18, P.W.16 has found the presence of Carbomate insecticide in blood and viscera of the deceased, no such substance was seized at the time of investigation.
As per Ex.P.17, the death was due to respiratory failure as a result of consumption of substance containing Carbomate insecticide.
As I have already discussed earlier, no such substance was found and seized by the I.O.

It is material to note that, the complainant and other relatives of the deceased have failed to identify the handwriting and signature found on Ex.P.3.
35.
To sumup, the complainant and other independent witnesses have denied the demand and receipt of dowry and alleged cruelty by the accused persons.
They are not aware, why the wife of the accused No.1 has committed suicide.
They are not aware of the cause of death.

Even as per Ex.P.17 &
Ex.P.18, there is a ambiguity about the cause of death of the deceased.
Admittedly, she had not sustained external injuries.
The prosecution case itself is doubtful.
Naturally, the accused persons are entitled to the benefit of doubt.
The available evidence is not sufficient to prove the guilt of the accused persons.
Hence, without any option, I answered all the points in the Negative.
36. Point No.5:

From the discussion made herein above, I proceed to pass the following:
O RDE R Acting under Section 235(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused persons are hereby acquitted of the offences punishable under Section 498A, 304B r/w 34 of Indian Penal Code and Sec.3 & 4 of D.P.Act.
The bail bond executed by the accused persons and the surety bond shall stand cancelled.
